justifications.functional_suitability: R-01, R-02, and R-03 are comprehensively covered by Claim Intake Wizard, Broker Portal Module, Adjuster Workspace, Claim Domain Model Component, and Dynamic Routing Policy Engine, fully supporting phased claim-type migration.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Meets R-05 (< 2s) by decoupling user queries from the slow mainframe using Claim Status & Audit Projection Component (CQRS), local data stores, and asynchronous transfers via Azure Service Bus and Outbox Processor Component.
justifications.compatibility: Fully accommodates legacy mainframe constraints via ACL Component, SFTP Sync Agent, and Mainframe Batch Staging Store without extending batch windows, alongside OIDC/OAuth2 integration with Corporate Active Directory.
justifications.usability: All user groups have dedicated interfaces: Claim Intake Wizard and Broker Portal Module for external submitters, and Adjuster Workspace with Sync Status Monitor and Offline State Manager for internal adjusters.
justifications.reliability: Guarantees zero claim loss and idempotency (R-04) using Outbox Processor Component, Azure Service Bus, Mainframe Batch Staging Store ledger, Relational Data Store ACID transactions, and Dead-Letter & Reconciliation Monitor.
justifications.security: Enforces SSO (R-07) via Authentication Component and JWT Validation Policy with Corporate Active Directory. Ensures accountability and integrity via Audit Trail Store (Temporal Tables) and SQL Database Ledger.
justifications.maintainability: R-06 is well supported via Dynamic Routing Policy Engine, App Config Lookup, and ACL Component for immediate rollback. However, running AKS adds operational complexity for a team with little cloud experience.
justifications.portability: Successfully bridges on-prem-mainframe and azure-westeurope using containerized .NET 8 services and SFTP, though components rely on Azure-proprietary services like Azure App Configuration and Azure API Management policies.

PERF-01.justification: CQRS read projections serve UI screens fast, but architecture lacks an explicit real-time cache or read-through strategy for data remaining exclusively on the mainframe.
sensitivity_points: Read performance depends on local projection freshness rather than synchronous mainframe calls
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of legacy claim data traded off against sub-2-second UI responsiveness

PERF-02.justification: Incoming claims are decoupled using Azure Service Bus and staged in the Ledger SQL database, buffering spikes without overloading the mainframe batch window.
sensitivity_points: Message queue buffering capacity during peak submission volumes
tradeoffs: Increased storage and queuing overhead traded off against protection of legacy batch processing

AVAIL-01.justification: Modern platform persists submissions locally and decouples legacy transmission using Outbox and Service Bus, resuming SFTP transfer whenever the mainframe batch window recovers.
sensitivity_points: Persistence reliability of the local outbox and batch staging store
tradeoffs: Temporary divergence of legacy records accepted to ensure high availability of intake

AVAIL-02.justification: Transactional outbox, SQL Ledger staging, and Dead-Letter & Reconciliation monitors protect against duplicate processing and data loss, though automated bidirectional reconciliation mechanics remain brief.
sensitivity_points: Reconciliation logic completeness and idempotency handling across SFTP batch transfers
tradeoffs: Operational overhead of dead-letter triage traded off against zero duplicate claims guarantee

MOD-01.justification: Dynamic routing policy in APIM and Azure App Configuration feature flags allow switching claim types between modern and legacy paths dynamically within minutes without mainframe redevelopment.
sensitivity_points: Granularity of routing rules maintained in Azure App Configuration
tradeoffs: Gateway routing policy complexity traded off against zero-downtime rollback capability

MOD-02.justification: Web client and adjusters communicate strictly with the API Gateway and Claims Core Service; legacy interaction is isolated via ACL and sync agents, avoiding UI refactoring.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling of frontend components from legacy data models via Domain-Driven Design
tradeoffs: Upfront ACL development cost traded off against long-term UI stability at cutover

SEC-01.justification: API Gateway enforces JWT validation and Developer Portal access, but broker-level resource isolation and fine-grained authorization checks are not explicitly specified in the components.
sensitivity_points: Claim-level tenancy enforcement within Claims Core Service domain logic
tradeoffs: Centralized gateway auth traded off against domain-level authorization policy enforcement

SEC-02.justification: Corporate AD SSO revokes platform access, but long-lived JWT token lifespans may exceed 15 minutes, and propagation of revocation to legacy mainframe accounts is unaddressed.
sensitivity_points: Token expiration/revocation policies and credential coupling between AD and mainframe
tradeoffs: JWT statelessness performance benefit traded off against prompt access revocation enforcement
